newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia says to expand kuna bond market.
newsitem.headline: Croatia says to expand kuna bond market.

text.p: Croatia said it planned to expand the domestic kuna bond market after launching an issue of 300 million kuna two-year Eurobonds on Wednesday.

"Over the next 12-18 months, the Ministry of Finance plans to develop further the medium term kuna bond market, with somewhat longer maturities and larger issue sizes," the ministry said in a statement faxed to Reuters.
It said the main focus in future would be on domestic retail placement. Croatian investors were expected to be drawn by attractive yields free of income tax.
The domestic market lacks safe long- and short-term instruments apart from 35-, 42- and 91-day T-bills.
By offering security of the principal, the ministry said it was "fostering an important process of capital formation in Croatia".
The former Yugoslav republic was among the first countries to issue Eurobonds denominated in the domestic currency.
"The acceptance of the kuna as a Eurobond currency by Euroclear, the international clearing and settlement system, is also an important advance for Croatia," it said.
The maiden issue carries a coupon of 12.5 percent with the issue price of 98.5 percent, maturing on December 18, 1998.
It was led by Merrill Lynch and Croatia's Zagrebacka Banka and syndicated equally at home and abroad.
Individual bonds are of the bearer type, each denominated at 10,000 kuna.
